items.name: Wiktionary (Indonesian edition)
items.role: Default source of Indonesian definitions, examples and syllable breaks.
items.note: Text is available under CC BY-SA 4.0 (and GFDL). Read straight from the browser through the Action API (it allows cross-origin reads), with the last answer kept in the browser for offline use. Community-written: coverage is uneven.
items.attribution: Definitions from id.wiktionary.org contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0; each entry links to its source page.

items.name: KBBI (optional)
items.role: Optional source of Indonesian definitions (off by default): word classes, example sentences and syllable breaks.
items.note: KBBI content belongs to Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa (Kemendikbudristek) and has no open licence. Off unless you choose it in Settings; then it is fetched by your own Kamus server from kbbi.web.id (a third-party site) or from a kbbi-api server you configure, for personal study only. Nothing from KBBI is distributed with Kamus. Requests to kbbi.web.id are throttled to 0.6 s apart.
items.attribution: © Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa, Kemendikbudristek; presented by kbbi.web.id.

items.name: Wiktionary (English edition)
items.role: English glosses, example translations, IPA, audio recordings and word suggestions. Titles of its Indonesian lemmas also form the word list the stemmer checks base words against.
items.note: Text is available under CC BY-SA 4.0 (and GFDL). Reuse needs attribution and the same licence. Read straight from the browser through the official REST and Action APIs (they allow cross-origin reads), with the last answer kept in the browser for offline use. A snapshot of the titles of its Indonesian lemmas (24,640 single words) ships as static/data/wordlist-id.txt for the stemmer; rebuild it with scripts/build_wordlist.py.
items.attribution: Definitions, examples and pronunciation by Wiktionary contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (en.wiktionary.org); reformatted for display.

items.name: Tatoeba
items.role: Extra Indonesian example sentences with English translations.
items.note: Sentences are mostly CC BY 2.0 FR (some CC0); each sentence carries its own licence and author in the API. Fetched by the browser from api.tatoeba.org/v1 (it sends CORS headers).
items.attribution: Sentences by Tatoeba contributors, CC BY 2.0 FR (some CC0); each sentence keeps its own author and licence.

items.name: Microsoft Edge read-aloud service (via edge-tts)
items.role: Neural voices id-ID-GadisNeural and id-ID-ArdiNeural for the edge-tts engine.
items.note: Unofficial access to the online service built into Microsoft Edge; it could change or stop at any time. Audio is cached locally.

items.name: Google Fonts
items.role: Serves the Roboto font to the page (falls back to the system font offline).

items.name: MyMemory
items.role: Optional engine that fills in missing translations of card text (Indonesian ↔ English).
items.note: Text you translate is sent to their server; anonymous use has a daily quota. Quality varies (it mixes translation memory and machine translation). Called directly from the browser (it sends CORS headers), so the text goes from your device to MyMemory without passing the Kamus server.

items.name: kbbi-api server (optional, not bundled)
items.license: MIT (code); data owned by Badan Bahasa
items.role: Optional KBBI source: any server that speaks the kbbi-api JSON format, named in KAMUS_KBBI_API_URL on the Kamus server.
items.note: Only used if you set it up. The project's own README says its data is owned by Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa and may not be used commercially.

items.name: AnkiWeb
items.role: Linked from the Anki page (opens in a new tab). Anki itself syncs your cards with it; Kamus never talks to AnkiWeb.

items.name: Firebase (Authentication + Firestore)
items.role: Optional: stores your cards and history in YOUR OWN Firebase project if you set up sync (Settings → Sync).
items.note: Off by default. Kamus has no Firebase project of its own; data goes from your browser to the project whose config you paste.

items.name: edge-tts
items.role: Python client for the Edge read-aloud service.

items.name: Wikidepia/indonesian-tts (model v1.2)
items.role: Offline Indonesian VITS voices (Wibowo, Ardi, Gadis). Three ways to run it: on the server (CPU), or converted to ONNX and run inside your browser; optional.
items.note: The repository has no licence file; its README says 'DO NOT USE FOR COMMERCIAL PURPOSES'. Fine-tuned on audiobook data and about 2,000 Azure TTS samples. VITS: Kim, Kong & Son (2021), arXiv:2106.06103. The ONNX file in models/wikidepia-v1.2/web/ is a derivative of this model (made by scripts/export_wikidepia_onnx.py) and carries the same non-commercial restriction.

items.name: Coqui TTS 0.8.0
items.role: Speech synthesis toolkit that runs the Wikidepia model (only inside .tts-env).
items.note: Installed from PyPI as TTS==0.8.0; later versions changed the model format, so it is pinned. It brings many dependencies (numpy, numba, librosa, pyworld, ...) that live only inside .tts-env; see `pip list` there for their licences.

items.name: onnxruntime-web
items.role: Runs the converted Wikidepia model inside the browser (WebAssembly build, served from static/vendor/ort/).
items.note: Copied from the npm package onnxruntime-web 1.31.1; licence taken from its package.json.

items.name: ONNX & onnxruntime (Python)
items.role: Used once, inside .tts-env, to export the model to ONNX and to check it against PyTorch (onnx 1.16.2, onnxruntime).
items.note: Not needed to run Kamus.

items.name: Wikidepia/g2p-id
items.role: Converts Indonesian text to IPA phonemes for the Wikidepia model (only inside .tts-env).
items.note: Installed from GitHub, not PyPI: the PyPI package 'g2p-id-py' is a different project with other output. It asks for Python 3.11+, so it is installed with --ignore-requires-python on 3.10. Stress marks and symbol fixes are added in wikidepia_worker.py.

items.name: python-crfsuite
items.role: Dependency of g2p-id (only inside .tts-env).

items.name: Argos Translate
items.role: Optional offline engine that translates card text (Indonesian ↔ English); runs in its own environment (.argos-env).
items.note: Dual-licensed MIT or CC0 (per its README). Its translation models (OpenNMT-based, from the Argos package index) are downloaded separately; their licence has not been verified.

items.name: Transformers.js
items.role: Runs the Opus-MT translation models inside the browser (static/vendor/transformers/, with its onnxruntime-web WebAssembly runtime).
items.note: Copied from the npm package @huggingface/transformers 4.3.2; licence taken from its package.json. It bundles onnxruntime-web (MIT).

items.name: Opus-MT id↔en (Helsinki-NLP; ONNX conversion by Xenova)
items.role: Offline translation models run in the browser (Settings → Translation → Opus-MT); served from models/opus-mt/ and stored in IndexedDB.
items.note: Apache-2.0 is the licence shown on the Helsinki-NLP model pages; the Xenova ONNX repositories show no licence field. They are trained on OPUS data, whose corpora carry their own licences. Downloaded by the browser from huggingface.co/Xenova (or from this server's copy).

items.name: LibreTranslate (server, not bundled)
items.role: Optional engine: any LibreTranslate server you host or can reach, set in Settings → Translation.
items.note: Kamus only talks to it over HTTP; no LibreTranslate code is included.

items.name: PyTorch & torchaudio (CPU builds 2.0.1 / 2.0.2)
items.role: Neural network runtime for Coqui TTS (only inside .tts-env).

items.name: Requests
items.role: HTTP client for KBBI, Wiktionary and Tatoeba.

items.name: sql.js
items.role: SQLite compiled to WebAssembly; writes the collection inside the .apkg export (static/vendor/apkg/).
items.note: Copied from the npm package sql.js 1.16.0 by scripts/fetch_vendor.sh; licence from its package.json.

items.name: JSZip
items.role: Writes the zip container of the .apkg export (static/vendor/apkg/).
items.note: Dual-licensed (MIT OR GPL-3.0-or-later) per its package.json; used under the MIT option.

items.name: Firebase JS SDK
items.role: Optional cloud sync: Google sign-in and Firestore in the browser (static/vendor/firebase/, compat bundles).
items.note: Copied from the npm package firebase 13.3.0 by scripts/fetch_vendor.sh; licence taken from its package.json (the package ships no LICENSE file). Loaded only when you add a Firebase config.

items.name: qrcode-generator
items.role: Draws the QR code that shares the sync settings with another device (static/vendor/qr/).
items.note: Copied from the npm package by scripts/fetch_vendor.sh; MIT is declared in its package.json and file header (no LICENSE file in the package).

items.name: jsQR
items.role: Reads that QR code from the camera in the in-app scanner (static/vendor/qr/).
items.note: Copied from the npm package jsqr 1.4.0 by scripts/fetch_vendor.sh.

items.name: Playwright (development only)
items.role: Runs the browser tests (viewport matrix, accessibility, task flows) in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox. Not part of the app.
items.note: devDependency @playwright/test; licence from its package.json.

items.name: axe-core (development only)
items.role: Accessibility rules engine used by the browser tests (through @axe-core/playwright). Not part of the app.
items.note: devDependencies @axe-core/playwright and axe-core; both declare MPL-2.0 in their package.json.

items.name: ESLint (development only)
items.role: Lints the JavaScript files and tests. Not part of the app.
items.note: devDependencies eslint, @eslint/js and globals; all declare MIT in their package.json.

items.name: TypeScript (development only)
items.role: Type-checks the JavaScript modules (checkJs, no build output). Not part of the app.
items.note: devDependency typescript; licence from its package.json.

items.name: AnkiConnect (Anki add-on, not bundled)
items.role: Optional. Lets this page add cards to, and read review progress from, Anki desktop on your own computer (add-on code 2055492159).
items.note: Kamus only talks to it over HTTP from your browser; no AnkiConnect code is included here.

items.name: Anki (desktop app, not bundled)
items.role: The flashcard app you practise in; Kamus creates notes in an Anki-compatible format (note type 'Kamus v1').
items.note: Anki is licensed AGPL-3.0 or later, with some parts BSD-3, MIT and CC BY 4.0.

items.name: Python standard library & SQLite
items.role: Web server, HTML parsing helpers and the lookup cache (SQLite is in the public domain).

items.name: Roboto
items.role: Typeface used throughout the page.

items.name: Material Symbols
items.role: Icons (search, history, settings, speaker, list, close...), embedded as inline SVG.

items.name: Material Design 3
items.role: Colours, shapes, navigation rail, side sheets, chips and typography follow Google's Material Design 3 guidelines.

items.name: Learning content (vocabulary, affix lessons, Malay/Indonesian differences, drills)
items.role: The starter word list, affix lessons, curated Indonesian/Malay differences and pronunciation drills shown on the Learn and Affixes pages (static/data/).
items.note: Written for Kamus. Hand-written from general knowledge of the languages: usage varies by region and register, so treat it as a guide and report mistakes. The live Malay comparison reads English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA).
